data.claim: A per-call as_agent is recorded for the harness so the same agent shell inherits it instead of deriving the tree name
data.falsifier: harness_identity.declared(repo, scope) returns "" after a call naming as_agent=sub-1
data.mechanism: _m_tools_call calls harness_identity.declare(repo, per_call, scope=session fingerprint) exactly as legacy ddflow_identify does (Bfad021e8d9)
data.question: Does a per-call as_agent name reach the agent own shell, or derive the tree name?

evidence.note: Research R54e5b687b6 CONFIRMED: a per-call as_agent name must be recorded for the harness (harness_identity.declare) so the agent own shell inherits it; regression test tests/test_review_shell_agent_name.py asserts H.declared(repo, scope)==sub-1 after an as_agent call.

Standing rules consulted (r-reuse-core: recording was already implemented by harness_identity.declare + ssddflow_identify Bfad021e8d9; reused, not reimplemented; r-adapters holds). ddflow recall of identity shell-inheritance precedent returned harness_identity/harnessreg + D-mcp-identity-per-call.
ddflow/surfaces/mcp/_handlers.py records the per-call as_agent via harness_identity.declare in _m_tools_call (commit 633214361); regression test tests/test_review_shell_agent_name.py added.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not exercise the shell/CLI path that the bug is about. It calls the MCP handler and then asserts that `harness_identity.declared` is `"sub-1"` in the same process/scope, but it never spawns a shell, never runs `ddflow review`, and never checks the review attribution or the CLI’s “you are …” output. Therefore, if the CLI still ignores `harness_identity`, or if the child shell’s session fingerprint differs from the MCP handler’s scope, the test still passes while `ddflow review` records the tree-derived name. This leaves the user-visible bug unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_shell_agent_name.py:38

chunk_findings.detail: The fix writes the per-call name into a single `(repo, session_fingerprint)` slot. If two MCP tool calls in the same server process carry different `as_agent` values and overlap — for example one MCP session runs `ddflow_brief as_agent="alice"` at the same time as another runs `ddflow_brief as_agent="bob"` — the second call’s `harness_identity.declare(...)` overwrites the first. Alice’s subsequently spawned shell then reads `harness_identity.declared(repo, scope=HR.session_fingerprint(os.environ))` and gets `bob`, so the review is still attributed to the wrong reviewer. The new test calls only one agent sequentially and cannot catch this interleaving.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp/_handlers.py:179

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test only asserts that the current process’s `H.declared(...)` returns `"sub-1"`; it never spawns the actual failing program, `ddflow review`, in a child shell. That means the test can pass even if the child process computes a different `HR.session_fingerprint(os.environ)` or the CLI still ignores `H.declared` and continues to derive `[hostname]-<item>-...`. It does not exercise the reported user-visible failure of B-ddflow-review-wrong-agent-name.
